title: Good DBMS_REDEFINITION usage — datatype change Oracle would otherwise reject
expected_feedback: No violations. Correct use of DBMS_REDEFINITION on a 50M-row table for a change Oracle rejects outright as a direct ALTER (ORA-01439 — a datatype class change needs an empty column), which is the case redefinition is actually for. num_errors is checked and raises rather than being printed and ignored, so a failed dependent-object copy cannot reach the cutover; DBA_REDEFINITION_ERRORS is named for triage. FINISH_REDEF_TABLE passes dml_lock_timeout explicitly, so the final swap neither aborts on the first concurrent DML nor waits indefinitely. Requires Enterprise Edition — state that dependency if the edition has not been confirmed.
